ਚਰਨ ਕਮਲ ਆਧਾਰੁ ਜਨ ਕਾ ਆਸਰਾ ॥:
The lotus feet of the Divine serve as the sole foundation and refuge for the humble servant. Absolute dependence upon that sacred presence is declared, affirming that every breath and hope rest within that shelter. The devotee finds life’s only anchorage through surrender to those beloved feet, praising the single support that sustains existence.

Themes: divine refuge, total dependence, lotus feet, shelter of the devotee, life's anchorage, humble surrender, sustaining presence, sacred support
ਚਰਨ ਕਮਲ ਸੇਵੀ ਰਿਦ ਅੰਤਰਿ ਗੁਰ ਪੂਰੇ ਕੈ ਆਧਾਰਿ:
The speaker vows to enshrine the Beloved’s lotus feet within the heart through simran (loving remembrance), resting wholly on the Perfect Guru as the only foundation and refuge. This is a first-person plea for grace to maintain that inward sanctuary, yoking the mind to divine presence through absolute surrender. The image of feet enshrined inside the self merges outward reverence with interior dwelling.

Themes: lotus feet as inner sanctuary, Perfect Guru as sole support and refuge, simran in the heart, plea for grace, absolute surrender, interior divine presence, merging outward reverence with inward dwelling
ਚਰਨ ਕਮਲ ਸਿਉ ਪ੍ਰੀਤਿ ਰੀਤਿ ਸੰਤਨ ਮਨਿ ਆਵਏ ਜੀਉ:
The rule of life centered on loving the lotus feet—symbols of the Divine presence and complete surrender—dwells within the minds of the saints. This defines the holy person as one whose inner nature is permanently anchored in devotion to the Beloved’s refuge. Sanctity is shown by an abiding attachment to sacred shelter rather than outward display.

Themes: lotus feet, divine love, saintly mind, rule of life, inner refuge, sacred presence, surrender, devotional custom
ਬੋਹਿਥੜਾ ਹਰਿ ਚਰਣ ਮਨ ਚੜਿ ਲੰਘੀਐ ॥:
Exhort your own mind to board the vessel formed by the Divine feet and cross the ocean of existence. The Punjabi reading addresses the mind, while the English speaks to a mortal. Those feet are refuge, transport, and the only sanctuary that ferries a soul from bondage to liberation. Climbing aboard is total surrender.

Themes: self-exhortation, Divine feet as refuge, vessel of liberation, crossing the world-ocean, sanctuary, surrender, deliverance from bondage
ਹਰਿ ਚਰਨ ਕਮਲ ਮਨੁ ਬੇਧਿਆ ਕਿਛੁ ਆਨ ਨ ਮੀਠਾ ਰਾਮ:
A mind pierced by the Lord’s lotus feet finds nothing else sweet, for simran (loving remembrance) alone saturates the heart. This proclaims a state of exclusive divine intoxication in which maya (worldly attachment) completely loses its flavor and every worldly pleasure turns hollow and insipid.

Themes: lotus feet piercing the mind, exclusive sweetness of divine remembrance, total loss of taste for maya, insipidity of worldly pleasures, singular devotion, divine intoxication, mind saturated with the Lord
ਪੀ ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤੁ ਆਘਾਨਿਆ ਗੁਰਿ ਅਮਰੁ ਕਰਾਇਆ ॥੨॥:
Drinking amrit (the ambrosial nectar of divine wisdom) brings total satiation and spiritual elevation; the Guru lifts the devotee into a deathless condition that never ages, never dies, and remains untouched by sorrow. It proclaims the fruit of receiving the Guru's gift, asserting that true immortality is a state beyond all temporal limits and pain.

Themes: spiritual elevation, deathless existence, divine nectar, Guru's grace, freedom from aging and sorrow, eternal satisfaction, transcendence of mortality
ਜਿਨ੍ਹ ਪੀਆ ਸੇ ਮਸਤ ਭਏ ਹੈ ਤੂਟੇ ਬੰਧਨ ਫਾਹੇ ॥:
Those who drink the sweet essence of naam (the divine Name) become utterly intoxicated and liberated; the fetters and snares of maya (worldly attachment) snap and fall away. Imbibing this sacred nectar dissolves every bond, and the enraptured soul attains total release. It celebrates liberation through divine rapture.

Themes: naam, divine intoxication, liberation from maya, shattering of bonds, ecstatic surrender, release from worldly fetters, spiritual drunkenness
ਹਰਿ ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤੁ ਸੋ ਚਖੈ ਮੇਰੇ ਮਨਾ ॥੨॥:
This instructs the mind to recognize that only those who taste the immortal nectar of the Lord’s naam (the divine Name) truly drink the water of spiritual life. Consuming that sacred Name is receiving divine sustenance, the nourishment that awakens the soul. It urges the only intake granting real existence.
Themes: naam, spiritual sustenance, tasting divine nectar, awakening of the soul, instruction to the mind, true life through the divine Name, drinking immortal nectar, inner urging
ਹਰਿ ਰਸੁ ਪੀਵਹੁ ਭਾਈ ॥:
Consume the Lord's sublime essence by taking refuge in the perfect Guru and chanting naam (the divine Name). The image of drinking is an exhortation to spiritually absorb divine nectar through devoted surrender to the Guru's shelter. Urges seekers to repeatedly imbibe that celestial intoxicant through guided remembrance rather than solitary effort.

Themes: Guru's refuge, naam (the divine Name), spiritual intoxication, devotional absorption, divine nectar, exhortation, surrender, guided practice.
ਗੁਰਿ ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤੁ ਹਰਿ ਮੁਖਿ ਚੋਇਆ ਮੇਰੀ ਜਿੰਦੁੜੀ:
The Guru pours the ambrosial nectar of naam (the divine Name) into the mouth of a soul perishing in spiritual death, resurrecting it into conscious divine life. The speaker celebrates a total reversal of inner mortality: one who was dying without the Name is restored to living awareness through the Guru’s life-giving sacrament.

Themes: spiritual death and resurrection, naam as ambrosial nectar, Guru’s restorative grace, reversal of inner mortality, awakening through the divine Name, sacramental initiation
ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤੁ ਨਾਮੁ ਨਿਧਾਨੁ ਹੈ ਮਿਲਿ ਪੀਵਹੁ ਭਾਈ ॥:
Naam (the divine Name) is an immortal treasure and healing nectar. Gather in sangat (the company of the devout) and drink this elixir together. It is an urgent summons to communal sustenance, framing divine remembrance as both a hoarded jewel and a shared draught that bestows deathless life through fellowship.

Themes: naam as ambrosial nectar, sangat and communal drinking, divine treasure, spiritual nourishment, collective devotion, immortality through remembrance, imperative to partake
ਜਨਮ ਮਰਣ ਭਉ ਕਟਿਓਨੁ ਫਿਰਿ ਜੋਨਿ ਨ ਪਾਏ ॥:
God severs the human being’s dread of birth and death, granting freedom so they never again enter the cycle of reincarnation. This proclaims final liberation from transmigration and the total extinction of mortal terror through divine intervention. The anxiety of dying and being reborn is cut away completely, and the endless rotation of womb-born lives finishes forever.

Themes: liberation from reincarnation, divine severance of birth-death fear, end of transmigration, eternal freedom from cyclical existence, removal of mortal dread, cessation of rebirth
ਸਹਜੁ ਭਇਆ ਪ੍ਰਭੁ ਪਾਇਆ ਜਮ ਕਾ ਭਉ ਲਥਾ ॥੨੦॥:
When the mind settles into sahaj (spontaneous spiritual poise), the Divine is realized and the terror of Jam, death's messenger, is lifted; spiritual death cannot come near. This declares that inner tranquility brings union with God and strips away mortal dread, replacing fear of perishing with fearless permanence in the Divine. Natural stillness achieves both presence of God and liberation from death's grip.

Themes: sahaj, spiritual poise, fear of death, union with God, inner stillness, spiritual death, divine realization, liberation from mortality
ਜਨਮ ਮਰਣ ਭਉ ਕਟੀਐ ਜਨ ਕਾ ਸਬਦੁ ਜਪਿ ॥:
The dread of birth and death—understood as the fear shadowing one's entire lifespan—is cut away by reciting praise-filled scripture, which the teeka explicitly locates within sangat (the company of the devout). Mortal anxiety dissolves through immersion in the Word; the terror spanning existence from birth to death is severed through this devotional chanting.

Themes: severing fear, birth and death, sangat, divine Word, praise, mortality, devotional recitation, existential liberation
ਨ ਦਨੋਤਿ ਜਸਮਰਣੇਨ ਜਨਮ ਜਰਾਧਿ ਮਰਣ ਭਇਅੰ ॥੧॥ ਰ:
Divine simran (loving remembrance) extinguishes the anguish born from the terror of birth, decay and dying. The declaration promises that constant remembrance severs the grip of existential dread, worry and anxiety, so the cycle of mortality ceases to torment the mind. This assurance of refuge declares that meditation on the Divine dissolves fear into peace.

Themes: simran, fear of death, existential dread, refuge, divine remembrance, peace, mortality, anxiety
ਜਨਮ ਮਰਣ ਦੁਖੁ ਕਾਟੀਐ ਪਿਆਰੇ ਚੂਕੈ ਜਮ ਕੀ ਕਾਣੇ:
In sangat (company of the devout), a lifetime’s anguish and the pain of birth and death are severed, and Death’s menace ends. The devotee is assured that holy fellowship annihilates worldly grief and mortal terror; communal refuge dissolves existential dread and the shadow of the grave.
Themes: sangat, liberation from birth and death, fear of death, end of suffering, holy fellowship, deliverance from Death, refuge in the devout, annihilation of grief
ਜਨਮ ਮਰਣ ਭੈ ਲਾਥੇ ॥੪॥੨॥੫੨॥:
All fears of birth and death have been completely erased, announcing liberation from the cycle of transmigration. The speaker declares fearless release from reincarnation, testifying that terror of repeated dying and rebirth has fully dissolved through spiritual attainment.

Themes: liberation from transmigration, end of reincarnation fear, spiritual freedom, existential fearlessness, cycle of birth and death, divine liberation, dissolution of dread, fearless attainment
ਸਾਧਸੰਗਤਿ ਕੈ ਆਸਰੈ ਪ੍ਰਭ ਸਿਉ ਰੰਗੁ ਲਾਏ ॥:
Taking refuge in sangat (the company of the devout) provides the shelter that ignites love for the Divine. The fellowship of the holy functions as an active support system that dyes the soul in affection for God. Remaining within that community, the individual enters into intimate union with the Beloved.

Themes: sangat, refuge, divine love, spiritual shelter, fellowship, devotion, union with the Divine
ਸਾਧੂ ਸੰਗਿ ਤਰੀਜੈ ਸਾਗਰੁ ਕਟੀਐ ਜਮ ਕੀ ਫਾਸਾ ਜੀ:
Association with the saints, sangat (the company of the devout), carries one across the ocean of worldly existence and slices apart death’s noose. Holy companionship functions as the vessel of liberation, severing mortality’s bonds and bringing the soul beyond the stormy sea of life. Refuge among the righteous annihilates the trap of death.

Themes: sangat, liberation, crossing the world-ocean, severing the noose of death, holy companionship, refuge, mortality
ਸਾਧਸੰਗਤਿ ਕੀ ਭੀਰ ਜਉ ਪਾਈ ਤਉ ਨਾਨਕ ਹਰਿ ਸੰਗਿ:
Joining the throng of the sangat (the company of the devout) brings the soul into direct encounter with the Divine. The speaker testifies from experience that finding the holy assembly causes union with God. A crowded gathering of saints is both a literal congregation and the gateway to meeting the Lord. Shared devotion in communal company results in merging with the Beloved.

Themes: sangat, divine union, holy assembly, communal devotion, meeting the Lord, spiritual gathering, encounter with the Divine
ਸੰਤਤ ਹੀ ਸਤਸੰਗਤਿ ਸੰਗ ਸੁਰੰਗ ਰਤੇ ਜਸੁ ਗਾਵਤ ਹ:
Those who abide continuously in sangat (the company of the devout) absorb the beautiful dye of celestial love and sing the Lord's praises without end, though the grammar stresses constant abiding rather than holy persons. They remain immersed in holy fellowship, saturated in divine affection, offering perpetual praise.

Themes: holy fellowship, divine saturation, celestial love-dye, ceaseless praise, spiritual immersion, devotion through sangat
ਕਾਢਿ ਲੀਏ ਪ੍ਰਭ ਆਨ ਬਿਖੈ ਤੇ ਸਾਧਸੰਗਿ ਮਨੁ ਲਾਵ:
Implores God to wrench the mind free from the poison of sensory objects and worldly distractions and bind it to the saadh sangat, the company of the devout. Presents divine power as the sole force that extracts consciousness from the grip of maya (worldly attachment) and anchors it in holy fellowship. The act is simultaneously rescue from corrupting entanglement and reorientation toward sacred community through complete surrender.

Themes: divine rescue from sensory poison, liberation through the company of the devout, God's agency in salvation, reorientation of consciousness, surrender of the mind, extraction from worldly entanglement, refuge in holy fellowship
ਮਹਿਮਾ ਸਾਧੂ ਸੰਗ ਕੀ ਸੁਨਹੁ ਮੇਰੇ ਮੀਤਾ ॥:
Call friends to heed the supreme greatness of sangat (the company of the devout), the sacred assembly of the Guru’s holy ones. This exhortation praises the transformative power of gathering with the saintly congregation and declares that communion with the devoted fellowship holds incomparable spiritual worth. The voice summons companions to listen with full attention to the glory inherent in united holy company.

Themes: sangat, holy company, spiritual assembly, attentive listening, Guru's congregation, glory of devotion, exhortation
ਮੇਰਾ ਗੁਰੁ ਪਰਮੇਸਰੁ ਸੁਖਦਾਈ ॥:
Declares the Guru to be the very form of the Transcendent Lord and the source of all peace. Affirms complete oneness between the living preceptor and the supreme reality that bestows every comfort. Proclaims that total refuge in the Guru delivers ultimate bliss because the guide is himself the divine giver of all wellbeing.

Themes: oneness of Guru and Divine, divine bestower of peace, spiritual refuge, source of all comfort, devotional realization, total surrender, supreme wellbeing
ਤੁਮ ਦਾਤੇ ਤੁਮ ਪੁਰਖ ਬਿਧਾਤੇ ॥:
Direct praise declares the Divine to be the sole creator of all beings, the consciousness pervading every creature, and the only giver of every gift. It acknowledges absolute dependence on one source for existence, immanence, and bounty, collapsing origin, presence, and provision into a single refuge. The speaker surrenders to the exclusive ordainer and all-pervading sovereign.

Themes: divine sovereignty, creation, omnipresence, immanence, total dependence, grace, surrender, sole refuge
ਕਰੁਣਾ ਮੈ ਕਿਰਪਾਲ ਕ੍ਰਿਪਾ ਨਿਧਿ ਜੀਵਨ ਪਦ ਨਾਨਕ:
The devotee pleads urgently with the merciful Lord, the treasure of compassion, to grant darshan (blessed vision of the Divine). This sight alone confers the exalted status of spiritual life and liberation-in-life, though English renderings sometimes read this redemption as already received rather than implored.

Themes: supplication for darshan, divine compassion as treasure, blessed vision bestowing spiritual life, liberation-in-life, mercy of the Lord, redemption through sight, pleading for grace
ਤੂੰ ਭਾਰੋ ਠਾਕੁਰੁ ਗੁਣੀ ਗਹੇਰਾ ॥੨॥:
Praise declares the Divine to be the great Lord and Master, utterly brimming with all virtue and immeasurably deep. The devotee bows before an inexhaustible treasury of excellence, though the teeka and translation diverge on whether this means deep-hearted profundity or stored riches. Worship addresses a goodness without limit and a nature profoundly beyond reach.

Themes: divine praise, lordship and surrender, infinite virtues, unfathomable depth, boundless excellence, transcendence, refuge in the Divine
ਦੇਵਣਹਾਰੁ ਦਾਤਾਰੁ ਕਿਤੁ ਮੁਖਿ ਸਾਲਾਹੀਐ ॥:
The speaker confronts the futility of praising the Divine Giver with a mere human mouth, admitting no creature can fully exhaust the praise of the One who sustains all. The teeka pushes the rhetorical question from individual humility to universal incapacity; every being falls short of completing that sifat (praise). The stance is awestruck surrender before limitless generosity.

Themes: inadequacy of human praise, divine generosity, humility before the Giver, universal limitation, sifat, surrender, rhetorical self-effacement, sustenance
ਤੇਰੇ ਕਵਨ ਕਵਨ ਗੁਣ ਕਹਿ ਕਹਿ ਗਾਵਾ ਤੂ ਸਾਹਿਬ ਗ:
The speaker confronts an inexhaustible storehouse of the Lord's virtues and admits that singing and recounting can never capture them all. The Lord is praised as sovereign Master, the treasure of all excellence, and the sustainer of everything. This is overwhelmed glorification, bowing before infinite goodness that forever exceeds every attempt at praise.

Themes: infinite divine virtues, glorification, divine sovereignty, treasure of excellence, inadequacy of language, praise and adoration, sustainer of all, overwhelmed devotion
ਰੇ ਬਉਰੇ ਤੁਹਿ ਘਰੀ ਨ ਰਾਖੈ ਕੋਈ ॥:
Admonishing the mind intoxicated by maya (worldly attachment), this warning declares that when death comes no relative will let you remain in their home even for a moment. The image of being cast out from the doorstep exposes the lie that family or wealth can shield the soul, revealing the total isolation of dying and the uselessness of looking to human ties for final refuge.

Themes: death, impermanence, abandonment by kin, solitude of the soul, futility of worldly shelter, maya, divine admonition, false security
ਕਾਹੇ ਮਨ ਤੂ ਡੋਲਤਾ ਹਰਿ ਮਨਸਾ ਪੂਰਣਹਾਰੁ ॥:
Stop wavering, O mind; the Divine fulfills every hope and desire. The self rebukes its own anxious oscillation between doubt and trust, insisting that the Lord who completes all yearning renders worry pointless. Restlessness dissolves before the certainty that every aspiration meets its completion in the One who answers longing.

Themes: reassurance, divine fulfillment, admonishing the mind, cessation of doubt, trust in providence, futility of anxiety
ਰੇ ਮਨ ਤੂ ਭੀ ਭਜੁ ਗੋਬਿੰਦ ॥੨॥:
The speaker turns inward to admonish his own mind, commanding it too to worship Gobind, the Lord of the Universe. This self-directed imperative treats the mind as a separate entity that must not lag behind but must join in active surrender and loving remembrance of the Divine. The insistence on inclusion presses the mind toward urgent participation in devotion, rejecting distraction and isolation from the source of liberation.

Themes: admonishing the mind, self-directed command, worship of Gobind, urgency of devotion, not being left behind, inward exhortation, divine remembrance, active spiritual participation
ਮਨ ਮੇਰਿਆ ਅੰਤਰਿ ਤੇਰੈ ਨਿਧਾਨੁ ਹੈ ਬਾਹਰਿ ਵਸਤੁ:
Admonishing the mind, it declares that the true treasure—God, the source of all bliss—already dwells within. The self holds the riches that the mind wrongly pursues through outward wandering in forests and wilderness. Turn inward; the fulfillment sought externally is already present inside. What seems distant is actually immanent.
Themes: inward turn, immanence of the Divine, futility of external seeking, self-knowledge, admonishing the mind, renunciation of outward pilgrimage, interior treasure
ਸੁਣਿ ਬਾਵਰੇ ਤੂ ਕਾਏ ਦੇਖਿ ਭੁਲਾਨਾ ॥:
Admonishment to a mind already maddened by maya (worldly attachment), commanding attention and asking why beholding that maya still makes it stray from life's path; the English implies the world caused the madness, but the teeka treats delusion as prior and the gaze as wandering. Urgent, confrontational, diagnostic: intoxication with the visible world is losing one's way.

Themes: admonition of the mind, maya as prior madness, straying from life's path, intoxication with the visible world, listening as command, diagnostic confrontation
ਸੁਣਿ ਬਾਵਰੇ ਥੀਉ ਰੇਣੁ ਜਿਨੀ ਪ੍ਰਭੁ ਧਿਆਇਆ ॥:
Admonishing the deluded mind with urgency, the command demands total ego-death: become the foot-dust of those who maintain simran (loving remembrance). This image of dissolving into the dust beneath the feet of the God-conscious declares that radical humility and complete self-erasure before the holy is the sole condition for attaining union with the Divine.

Themes: ego annihilation, humility, dust of the devotees, simran, divine union, self-effacement, surrender to the holy, prerequisite for God-realization
ਲਖ ਖੁਸੀਆ ਪਾਤਿਸਾਹੀਆ ਜੇ ਸਤਿਗੁਰੁ ਨਦਰਿ ਕਰੇਇ:
One merciful glance of grace (nadar) from the True Guru (satguru) gives the seeker the felt sense of owning the happiness of countless empires. It declares that royal luxury is nothing compared to the fulfillment of receiving the Guru’s favor, praising that single look as the supreme wealth and the true source of limitless inner joy.

Themes: grace of the True Guru, divine glance, inner sovereignty surpassing kingship, worldly pleasure as hollow, spiritual fulfillment, true wealth, transformative mercy
ਸਤਿਗੁਰੁ ਹੋਇ ਦਇਆਲੁ ਤਾ ਦੁਖੁ ਨ ਜਾਣੀਐ ॥:
When the True Guru (the enlightened guide) shows mercy, the devotee no longer registers suffering as suffering. Pain may still appear, yet it carries no sting because grace has dissolved its power. This describes the transformed awareness that results from divine compassion: affliction is redefined for one sheltered by the Guru's kindness.

Themes: divine mercy, transformed perception of suffering, grace that dissolves affliction, shelter of the True Guru, non-recognition of pain, subjective experience of hardship
ਹਰਿ ਚਉਥੜੀ ਲਾਵ ਮਨਿ ਸਹਜੁ ਭਇਆ ਹਰਿ ਪਾਇਆ ਬਲਿ:
The soul-bride completes the fourth nuptial round and attains the divine marriage she longed for. Her mind settles into sahaj (effortless spiritual poise), discovering the Lord through grace. She declares total surrender, a sacrifice of love fulfilled, proclaiming that sacred stillness and union have finally arrived.

Themes: nuptial union, sahaj, divine realization, surrender, spiritual marriage, grace, inner equipoise, devotion
ਸੁਖੁ ਪਾਇਆ ਸਤਿਗੁਰੂ ਮਨਾਇ ॥:
Establishing the True Guru within the heart harvests every desired fruit and brings unshakable peace. Heart-deep surrender to the divine guide completes the seeker. This declares that making sacred wisdom dwell inside replaces all inner lack with wholeness and that true ease is found through internal devotion rather than outward show.

Themes: inner surrender, divine peace, heart as sanctuary, fruition of desires, indwelling of the True Guru, wholeness through devotion, removal of inner lack
ਸਤਿਗੁਰੁ ਮੇਰਾ ਸਦਾ ਸਹਾਈ ਜਿਨਿ ਦੁਖ ਕਾ ਕਾਟਿਆ:
The True Guru is eternal refuge and support for those who seek sanctuary. He severs the banner of pain and destroys the root of sorrow entirely. The speaker declares that divine help has become permanent because suffering has been uprooted at its source, not merely eased but obliterated. This is praise and gratitude for the Guru who annihilates the very foundation of grief.

Themes: eternal divine support, destruction of suffering at its root, refuge and sanctuary, gratitude for the Guru, annihilation of pain, liberation through surrender, permanent help
ਗੋਬਿੰਦ ਮਿਲਣ ਕੀ ਇਹ ਤੇਰੀ ਬਰੀਆ ॥:
Your life is a brief, unrepeatable opening to meet Gobind, the Lord of the Universe. The stance is urgent admonition, warning you not to squander this rare chance for divine union because the window for God-realization will not remain open.
Themes: fleeting opportunity, divine union, urgency of spiritual pursuit, impermanence of life, meeting the Divine, seizing the moment, human purpose, God-realization
ਪ੍ਰਾਣੀ ਤੂੰ ਆਇਆ ਲਾਹਾ ਲੈਣਿ ॥:
The mortal came into this world to extract a spiritual gain, specifically naam, the divine Name, rather than worldly accumulation. This warning frames human life as a temporary journey whose only valid currency is remembrance of the Divine. It insists that the entire purpose of this brief birth is to amass imperishable earnings through devotion before departure.

Themes: purpose of human life, spiritual profit, naam (the divine Name), impermanence, worldly detachment, divine remembrance, true earnings, admonition
ਹਰਿ ਭਗਤਿ ਦ੍ਰਿੜੁ ਮਿਲੁ ਸਾਧ ਨਾਨਕ ਤੇਰੈ ਕਾਮਿ:
Seek the saadh (the holy person, or sangat, the company of the devout) and make bhagti (devotional worship) immovably firm within the heart. Only this inwardly anchored practice truly serves your purpose. Meeting the holy implants devotion; that alone yields lasting utility. Nothing else will avail you.

Themes: holy company, firm devotion, inner worship, true utility, seeking the Guru, heart's anchoring, what serves, lasting purpose
ਜੀਵਨਾ ਸਫਲ ਜੀਵਨ ਸੁਨਿ ਹਰਿ ਜਪਿ ਜਪਿ ਸਦ ਜੀਵਨਾ:
Existence becomes fruitful and deathless only when a person hears the divine Name (naam) and sustains continuous jap (devotional repetition) and simran (loving remembrance). This declares the criterion for a successful life: receptive listening and unbroken repetition of the sacred word transform biological survival into eternal spiritual vitality. True accomplishment in living is found through auditory devotion and ceaseless meditation, not through mere longevity.

Themes: fruitful existence, eternal life, hearing the divine Name, jap and simran, criterion for success, spiritual vitality, true accomplishment, devotional listening
ਸੰਤ ਜਨਾ ਕੀ ਰੇਣੁਕਾ ਲੈ ਮਾਥੈ ਲਾਵਉ ॥੧॥ ਰਹਾਉ:
The speaker begs for the dust of the saints’ feet to place upon the forehead, counting that blessing as greater than the nine treasures and the eighteen siddhis (supernatural powers). They plead for this gift as the sole wealth and perfection, preferring the company of the devout (sangat) over every worldly or miraculous attainment. Though the English suggests an accomplished act, the teeka reads it as an aspiration.

Themes: dust of the saints, humility, spiritual wealth, sangat, plea for grace, surrender, devotion, supremacy of holy company over occult powers
ਗੁਰਸਿਖਾਂ ਕੀ ਹਰਿ ਧੂੜਿ ਦੇਹਿ ਹਮ ਪਾਪੀ ਭੀ ਗਤਿ:
The speaker pleads as a self-confessed sinner for the dust of the feet of the Guru’s Sikhs, the sangat (company of the devout), believing that such humble residue carries the power to elevate a corrupt soul to a lofty spiritual state. The stance is desperate supplication, asserting that nearness to the holy is the sole refuge for the wicked and that even the unworthy may attain liberation through this contact.

Themes: humility, sangat, grace through association, salvation of sinners, dust of the feet, spiritual elevation, supplication
ਕਰਉ ਨਮਸਕਾਰ ਭਗਤ ਜਨ ਧੂਰਿ ਮੁਖਿ ਲਾਵਉ ॥੩॥:
The speaker pleads with utter humility, begging to bow before the devotees and press the dust of their feet to his face; this is the outward form of his prayer that he may enter the sangat (company of the devout), dwell among the holy, and join their song of divine praise. The stance is urgent supplication, treating the saints as the very doorway to the Divine.

Themes: reverence for the devotees, dust of the saints' feet as token of humility and refuge, yearning for sangat, prayer to join the holy congregation, singing divine praise in the company of saints, self-abnegation before the devout, saints as the path to God
ਟਹਲ ਕਰਉ ਤੇਰੇ ਦਾਸ ਕੀ ਪਗ ਝਾਰਉ ਬਾਲ ॥:
The speaker begs for the grace to serve the Lord’s own servant, wiping the dust from that devotee’s feet with his hair. This declares that the highest worship is absolute self-abasement, erasing all pride by treating the lowliest service to the Divine’s slave as the most precious privilege.
Themes: humility, egolessness, service to the Lord’s servant, surrender, devotion through menial service, reverence for the devout, self-effacement, divine love.
ਕਰਿ ਕਿਰਪਾ ਧੂਰਿ ਦੇਹੁ ਸੰਤਨ ਕੀ ਸੁਖੁ ਨਾਨਕੁ ਇ:
The devotee pleads personally for himself, begging for the dust falling from the feet of the saints as the supreme gift of grace. The stance is one of absolute self-abasement and longing, seeking peace not through direct approach but through the lowest trace of the holy, finding bliss in the very remnants left by the devout.

Themes: dust of the saints' feet, supreme grace, personal supplication, utter humility, yearning for peace, refuge in sanctity, self-abasement, devotional longing
ਸੰਤਹ ਚਰਣ ਹਮਾਰੋ ਮਾਥਾ ਨੈਨ ਦਰਸੁ ਤਨਿ ਧੂਰਿ ਪਰ:
The speaker pleads for unbroken intimacy with the Saints: forehead ever resting at their feet, eyes continually beholding their blessed vision, body perpetually covered in the dust of their feet. It is a prayer for complete ego-death through relentless nearness to the holy, asking that every faculty be absorbed in reverent contact with the devout and sanctified.

Themes: surrender to the Saints, ego annihilation, blessed vision, holy dust, humility, constant devotion, sanctification through presence, service to the devout
ਅਤਿ ਸੁੰਦਰ ਮਨਮੋਹਨ ਪਿਆਰੇ ਸਭਹੂ ਮਧਿ ਨਿਰਾਰੇ ॥:
Praise directed to the supremely beautiful mind-bewitching Beloved declares the One who dwells within all yet remains utterly distinct. The teeka reads these glorifying words as spiritually life-giving rather than mere description. It is adoration asserting divine immanence and transcendence together, declaring that such praise animates the soul.

Themes: divine immanence and transcendence, praise as spiritual sustenance, the mind-bewitching Beloved, presence within all yet utterly distinct, glorification animating the soul, captivating beauty of the Divine
ਤੇਰਾ ਨਾਮੁ ਰੂੜੋ ਰੂਪੁ ਰੂੜੋ ਅਤਿ ਰੰਗ ਰੂੜੋ ਮੇ:
The speaker exclaims in ecstatic praise, overwhelmed by the flawless beauty of the Beloved encountered through naam (the divine Name), sacred form, and intoxicating divine love. Every avenue of knowing God—heard, beheld, and felt—proves ravishing beyond compare. The declaration anchors devotion in sheer aesthetic wonder and commands the heart to pause, arrested by overwhelming loveliness.

Themes: divine beauty, naam (the divine Name), ecstatic praise, the sacred form of the Beloved, intoxicating divine love, aesthetic wonder, commanding the heart to pause, overwhelming loveliness
ਸੁੰਦਰ ਰਸਾਲ ਤੂ ॥੧॥:
The Divine is addressed directly as surpassingly beautiful and as the living source of all spiritual nectar. The voice praises and confesses that every blissful essence flows from that presence alone. God is not merely attractive but the origin of the sweetness that saturates devotion, the wellspring of all savor and spiritual flavor that devotees receive.

Themes: divine beauty, source of nectar, praise, devotional confession, spiritual bliss, God's sweetness, sacred essence
ਨੈਣ ਪਸੰਦੋ ਸੋਇ ਪੇਖਿ ਮੁਸਤਾਕ ਭਈ ॥:
The eyes drink in the Beloved’s overwhelming beauty and are utterly bewitched; the speaker declares a state of intoxicated rapture, where sheer beholding melts awareness into ecstatic surrender. Sight becomes the gateway to enraptured longing, and gazing upon that presence leaves the heart completely absorbed, spellbound, and thirsting.

Themes: divine beauty, enraptured vision, intoxicated devotion, ecstatic surrender, spellbound heart, mystical longing, the gaze of love
ਸੁੰਦਰ ਸੋਭਾ ਲਾਲ ਗੋਪਾਲ ਦਇਆਲ ਕੀ ਅਪਰ ਅਪਾਰਾ ਰ:
The radiant splendor of the Beloved Lord of the universe, the abode of mercy, spreads everywhere as beauty without end, though whether boundlessness belongs to the glory or the Divine remains unclear. That glory is immeasurable, limitless, and infinitely pervading. Praise declares the unfathomable magnificence of the compassionate Beloved.
Themes: divine glory, infinite beauty, mercy of the Beloved, boundless splendor, pervading presence, praise of the Lord
ਅਪੁਨੇ ਸੇਵਕ ਕੀ ਆਪੇ ਰਾਖੈ ਆਪੇ ਨਾਮੁ ਜਪਾਵੈ ॥:
The Divine Himself preserves the honor of His servant everywhere, and He Himself places His naam (the divine Name) upon the devotee's tongue. This declares that both dignity and devotion flow from grace alone; the Beloved shields the servant's standing and also supplies the very impulse to simran (loving remembrance). No self-effort creates either safety or spiritual utterance.

Themes: divine protection of honor, naam (the divine Name), simran (loving remembrance), total dependence on grace, absence of self-effort, divine initiative in devotion
ਭਗਤ ਜਨਾ ਕੀ ਹਰਿ ਜੀਉ ਰਾਖੈ ਜੁਗਿ ਜੁਗਿ ਰਖਦਾ ਆ:
The Divine eternally upholds the honor of devotees across every age, declaring an unbroken guardianship that praises the Creator’s faithfulness. God guards the dignity of the faithful through all time, never forsaking those who surrender. Age after age, the Divine sustains the standing of servants who trust in that refuge.

Themes: divine protection, eternal honor, preservation of devotees, timeless guardianship, dignity of the faithful, unbroken refuge, praise of divine faithfulness
ਭਗਤ ਤੇਰੇ ਸਭਿ ਪ੍ਰਾਣਪਤਿ ਪ੍ਰੀਤਮ ਤੂੰ ਭਗਤਨ ਕਾ:
Declares a reciprocal belovedness between the Divine and the bhagat (devotee): the Lord, the beloved master of life, is cherished by all devotees, and the devotees are themselves dear to the Lord. Praises the mutual intimacy binding the life-giver and the faithful in a two-way bond of love.

Themes: reciprocal belovedness, mutual love, divine intimacy, lord of life, two-way devotion, inseparable bond, faithful belovedness, bhagat
ਭਗਤਾ ਕੀ ਟੇਕ ਤੂੰ ਸੰਤਾ ਕੀ ਓਟ ਤੂੰ ਸਚਾ ਸਿਰਜਨ:
The True Creator is praised as the immovable pillar and shielding roof for the devoted. Following the teeka, the naam (the divine Name) itself constitutes this refuge, bearing up worshippers and sheltering saints alike. The utterance proclaims total reliance on God, identifying the Lord with His Name as the single, all-sufficient sanctuary.

Themes: refuge, divine Name, total dependence, shelter of saints, True Creator, worshipper's support, surrender
ਹਰਿ ਜੁਗੁ ਜੁਗੁ ਭਗਤ ਉਪਾਇਆ ਪੈਜ ਰਖਦਾ ਆਇਆ ਰਾਮ:
The Divine generates devotees in every epoch and age, and in moments of crisis or hostile pressure actively safeguards their dignity and honor. Declaring unbroken divine faithfulness, it affirms that protection persists through cyclical time and that the Creator defends the honor of the devout when they are most vulnerable.

Themes: divine protection across ages, preservation of honor in crisis, cyclical time, creation of devotees, faithfulness through epochs, shelter under oppression, eternal guardianship
ਹਮਰੇ ਕਰਮ ਨ ਬਿਚਰਹੁ ਠਾਕੁਰ ਤੁਮ੍ਹ ਪੈਜ ਰਖਹੁ ਅ:
A slave falls at the Master's feet begging Him not to weigh or audit his good and evil deeds, for the servant has none to offer; instead the supplicant clings to the Lord's own honor and reputation, pleading that the Master Himself preserve the dignity of His dependent. It is a cry for unearned mercy that bypasses the ledger of actions and banks entirely on the protector's pride in His own household.

Themes: pleading for mercy, unexamined actions, grace over justice, honor of the dependent, divine protection, servant's helplessness, master's reputation
ਜਾਚਿਕੁ ਮੰਗੈ ਨਿਤ ਨਾਮੁ ਸਾਹਿਬੁ ਕਰੇ ਕਬੂਲੁ ॥:
The devotee who adopts the posture of a beggar and pleads persistently for naam (the divine Name) receives certain acceptance from the Sovereign Lord. This is a declaration that relentless, humble petition for the Name moves the Master to grant the prayer. Complete dependence and daily supplication secure divine approval; God does not reject the soul that asks in perpetual need.
Themes: begging posture, persistent daily prayer, naam as the sole request, divine acceptance of the supplicant, total surrender to the Master, grace for the humble petitioner, spiritual poverty as a virtue
ਦੇਹਿ ਨਾਮੁ ਸੰਤੋਖੀਆ ਉਤਰੈ ਮਨ ਕੀ ਭੁਖ ॥:
A devotee begs God to bestow naam (the divine Name), trusting that this gift alone will quench the soul's restless craving and fill the mind with lasting contentment. The plea frames spiritual hunger as an acute inner famine that only the Name can satisfy, tying the reception of grace directly to the end of mental desire and the birth of true satisfaction.

Themes: supplication, divine Name as sustenance, contentment through grace, cessation of mental craving, spiritual hunger, satisfaction of the soul
ਜਾਚਿਕੁ ਨਾਮੁ ਜਾਚੈ ਜਾਚੈ ॥:
A beggar pleads repeatedly for naam (the divine Name), acknowledging God as the sole support of all beings, their only master, and the giver of every peace. The stance is one of absolute dependence and urgent, persistent supplication, stripping away all self-sufficiency to ask for the only gift that sustains. The soul begs as one utterly without resources before the single source of all refuge and comfort.

Themes: supplication, begging for naam, divine refuge, total surrender, dependence on God, repeated pleading, God as sole support, God as giver of peace
ਕਰਹੁ ਕ੍ਰਿਪਾ ਗੋਪਾਲ ਗੋਬਿਦੇ ਅਪਨਾ ਨਾਮੁ ਜਪਾਵਹ:
The devotee begs the Life of the World and Lord of the Universe for mercy, pleading to be empowered to chant the naam (divine Name). Without divine aid, simran (loving remembrance) cannot begin; the capacity to remember must be bestowed. This admits total dependence, framing devotion as a gift granted only by grace.
Themes: grace enabling naam, divine empowerment of simran, remembrance depending on mercy, prayer for devotion as gift, helplessness without grace, surrender to the Life of the World
ਜਾਚਕੁ ਮੰਗੈ ਦਾਨੁ ਦੇਹਿ ਪਿਆਰਿਆ ॥:
The speaker adopts the posture of a destitute beggar, hands outstretched, pleading with the Beloved for the gift of naam (the divine Name). This is an act of complete surrender and raw vulnerability, stripping away every trace of pride to ask for grace alone. It frames spiritual life as dependence on divine charity rather than personal merit.

Themes: begging for grace, surrender to the Divine, gift of naam, spiritual poverty, humility as refuge, divine charity, love-longing
ਦਰਿ ਮੰਗਤੁ ਜਾਚੈ ਦਾਨੁ ਹਰਿ ਦੀਜੈ ਕ੍ਰਿਪਾ ਕਰਿ:
The self is a destitute beggar at the Divine door, pleading for alms and charity. Utter dependence on the Lord’s kirpa (divine grace) frames the request: only through mercy can the gift be received. The stance is abject supplication and surrender, acknowledging that the soul owns nothing and must be given everything.

Themes: supplication, divine grace, humility, surrender, begging at the door, dependence on kirpa, spiritual poverty, receiving divine charity
ਮਉਲਿਓ ਮਨੁ ਤਨੁ ਹੋਇਓ ਹਰਿਆ ਏਕ ਬੂੰਦ ਜਿਨਿ ਪਾਈ:
Receiving even one drop of naam (the divine Name) as spiritual water makes the mind blossom and the body turn green like parched earth reviving after rain, declaring how minimal divine contact transforms the whole being from inner drought to lush aliveness through one sip of sacred water.

Themes: naam, spiritual renewal, mind-body transformation, divine grace, inner blossoming, scarcity to abundance, revitalization
ਹਰਿ ਰਸੁ ਪੀਵਤ ਸਦ ਹੀ ਰਾਤਾ ॥:
One who drinks the nectar of naam (the divine Name) remains forever dyed in its hue; the passage declares that imbibing this divine elixir produces permanent intoxication and irreversible saturation. It reveals that tasting the Lord's essence colors every moment with ceaseless presence and rapture, leaving the drinker eternally imbued.

Themes: naam, divine intoxication, permanent spiritual saturation, nectar of remembrance, eternal imbued state, drinking the divine essence, irreversible dyeing of the soul, ceaseless divine presence
ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤ ਰਸੁ ਕੀਰਤਨੁ ਹਰਿ ਗਾਈਐ ਅਹਿਨਿਸਿ ਪੂਰਨ:
Make the Lord's kirtan (congregational praise) your song, for it is the true amrit ras (nectar of immortality); within the singer, day and night, the naad (primal sound-current) of spiritual bliss resounds without end. The instruction urges turning all effort toward divine praise and promises that this practice fills the soul with an unbroken inner music of perfect fulfillment and celestial joy.

Themes: kirtan, naad, amrit ras, inner resonance, ceaseless practice, spiritual bliss, spiritual life
ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤੁ ਰਸਨਾ ਪੀਉ ਪਿਆਰੀ ॥:
Addressing one's own tongue as a beloved companion, the speaker issues a tender command to imbibe the deathless nectar of naam (the divine Name). The image of drinking sweet ambrosia turns the physical organ of speech into an instrument of spiritual survival, urging it to taste the elixir that sustains the soul rather than wasting itself on empty words. It is self-directed instruction that treats devotion as nourishment.

Themes: naam, ambrosial nectar, tongue as spiritual instrument, self-instruction, loving remembrance, soul's nourishment, speech as devotion
ਤੇਰਾ ਜਨੁ ਰਾਮ ਰਸਾਇਣਿ ਮਾਤਾ ॥:
The Lord's servant stays perpetually intoxicated, fully submerged in the divine elixir of naam (the divine Name). This affirms the devotee's total absorption in sacred rapture, portraying remembrance as an inebriating essence that yields unbroken ecstasy and complete self-abandonment into the Beloved.

Themes: spiritual intoxication, divine elixir, naam, ecstatic absorption, total surrender, devotee's state, sacred rapture, inebriating essence
ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤੁ ਰਸੁ ਪੀਆ ਗੁਰ ਸਬਦੀ ਹਮ ਨਾਮ ਵਿਟਹੁ ਕ:
The speaker declares that through the Guru's Word they imbibe the ambrosial nectar of spiritual life, becoming a sacrifice to the naam (the divine Name). This is an exclamation of total surrender, stating that the transformative essence received through sacred instruction provokes absolute self-offering. Gratitude and devotion consume the self entirely, dedicating existence to the life-giving Name.

Themes: ambrosial nectar, total surrender to the divine Name, Guru's Word as conduit of grace, self-sacrifice, spiritual transformation through divine sweetness, devotion, gratitude
ਰਸੁ ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤੁ ਨਾਮੁ ਰਸੁ ਅਤਿ ਭਲਾ ਕਿਤੁ ਬਿਧਿ:
The divine Name, naam, is the most sublime ambrosial essence, the nectar that gives spiritual life and sustains the soul. This declaration praises the supreme taste while pleading for the method by which a human can obtain and consume this essence. How can anyone receive this highest ras that revives the inner being?

Themes: naam as supreme ambrosial essence, nectar that gives spiritual life, yearning to taste the divine, method of obtaining the Name, sustenance for the soul, revival of the inner being
ਬਿਖੈ ਬਨੁ ਫੀਕਾ ਤਿਆਗਿ ਰੀ ਸਖੀਏ ਨਾਮੁ ਮਹਾ ਰਸੁ:
Addressing the self as a companion, the utterance commands abandoning the flat, unsatisfying water of sensual vice and worldly corruption to instead imbibe the intensely sweet nectar of naam (the divine Name). It juxtaposes two drinks to declare that only divine remembrance yields true savor, insisting on an absolute exchange of hollow indulgence for the rich intoxication of spiritual absorption.

Themes: renunciation of vice, insipidity of worldly corruption, nectar of naam (the divine Name), divine remembrance as sustenance, imperative counsel to the soul, spiritual intoxication, contrast between sensory and divine flavor
ਕਬੀਰ ਬਿਰਹੁ ਭੁਯੰਗਮੁ ਮਨਿ ਬਸੈ ਮੰਤੁ ਨ ਮਾਨੈ ਕ:
The serpent of birha (love-longing for the Divine) dwells in the mind that has entered the Guru's shelter, and no mantra can pacify it. The image treats genuine spiritual separation not as a sickness to be cured by ritual technique but as an overwhelming force that consumes every method. This is the irrepressible ache of a self seized by longing for union.

Themes: birha (divine separation), the Guru's shelter, uncontrollable spiritual longing, futility of ritual mantras, serpent of separation, all-consuming love, inner ache beyond technique, irrepressible yearning for union
ਹਰਿ ਬਿਨੁ ਕਿਉ ਜੀਵਾ ਮੇਰੀ ਮਾਈ ॥:
A desperate cry to one's mother confessing that survival is impossible without naam (the divine Name). The teeka reads the agony as separation from the Name rather than from the Divine directly; the soul grows tormented and restless when that remembrance is absent, and existence itself withers. This is an intimate lament of absolute dependence, treating divine connection as life's bare necessity rather than optional solace.

Themes: separation from naam, existential desperation, soul's restlessness, absolute dependence on divine remembrance, intimate lament, spiritual survival
ਪ੍ਰਭ ਮਿਲਬੇ ਕਉ ਪ੍ਰੀਤਿ ਮਨਿ ਲਾਗੀ ॥:
Love for the Divine Beloved has been born in the mind, declaring an urgent, intimate longing for union. This is not gentle fondness but an ardent, consuming desire to meet the Lord face to face. The inward self has been seized by devoted yearning, initiating a transformation through raw spiritual desire.

Themes: birth of divine love in the mind, urgent longing for union with the Beloved, intimate devotion, ardent desire for face-to-face meeting, inward self seized by yearning, transformation through spiritual desire
ਹਰਿ ਦਰਸਨ ਕਉ ਮੇਰਾ ਮਨੁ ਬਹੁ ਤਪਤੈ ਜਿਉ ਤ੍ਰਿਖਾ: The mind burns unbearably for darshan (the blessed Vision of the Divine), comparing that torment to a thirsty person without water. It voices desperate pleading, confessing total dependency and an agonizing thirst that only the Beloved’s presence can satisfy. Themes: longing for darshan, spiritual thirst, divine absence, desperate pleading, surrender through need, inner burning, separation from the Beloved
ਬਾਝਹੁ ਪਿਆਰੇ ਕੋਇ ਨ ਸਾਰੇ ਏਕਲੜੀ ਕੁਰਲਾਏ ॥:
Without the Beloved, no one cares for the soul; it cries utterly alone in the world that is a desolate jungle. The image of solitary weeping exposes total dependence on the Divine and the worthlessness of every other refuge. This is a raw lament of abandonment, pleading for the sole Partner who can rescue the isolated being.

Themes: divine abandonment, existential loneliness, the world as wilderness, the soul's helplessness, dependence on the Beloved, yearning in separation, the futility of worldly refuge
ਮਨਿ ਬੈਰਾਗੁ ਭਇਆ ਦਰਸਨੁ ਦੇਖਣੈ ਕਾ ਚਾਉ ॥:
The mind has grown feverish with love for the Divine and burns with an urgent thirst to receive darshan (the blessed sight of the Beloved’s presence). Declaring an inward condition of total absorption, it voices the soul’s restless longing to behold God directly, affirming that the heart now exists solely for the moment of intimate encounter with the Absolute.

Themes: divine love, viraha, longing for darshan, spiritual thirst, inner awakening, direct vision of God, devotion, beatific presence
ਘਰਿ ਆਵਹੁ ਚਿਰੀ ਵਿਛੁੰਨਿਆ ਮਿਲੁ ਸਬਦਿ ਗੁਰੂ ਪ੍:
A soul separated from God for ages pleads as a bride to her Divine Husband to come dwell within her heart-home. The speaker begs for reunion and intimate indwelling, not merely a distant meeting, asking that union be granted through the Guru's Word. The stance is urgent, vulnerable longing: the devotee acknowledges prolonged exile from the Beloved and presses the Lord to enter the inner sanctuary and restore the broken marital union.

Themes: longing for reunion, bridal mysticism, separation from the Divine, Guru's Word as the means of union, pleading with the Beloved, God dwelling within the heart, restoration of unity, the soul as a separated bride.
ਪਿਰ ਦੋਸੁ ਨਾਹੀ ਸੁਖਹ ਦਾਤੇ ਹਉ ਵਿਛੁੜੀ ਬੁਰਿਆਰ:
The soul absolves her Husband Lord, the Giver of peace, of all blame for their estrangement, admitting that her own evil deeds caused the separation. She completely exonerates the Beloved and accepts the rupture as her own fault. This is a direct confession that alienation from the Divine is self-inflicted through personal wrongdoing rather than any failure of the Giver of bliss.
Themes: blameless Beloved, soul as bride, self-caused separation, confession of guilt, spiritual estrangement, evil conduct, Giver of peace, rupture from the Divine
ਆਉ ਜੀ ਤੂ ਆਉ ਹਮਾਰੈ ਹਰਿ ਜਸੁ ਸ੍ਰਵਨ ਸੁਨਾਵਨਾ:
The devotee invites the Beloved Guru to come and dwell within the heart’s inner home so the ears may receive har jas (the Lord’s Praises) through sravana (sacred hearing). The supplicant begs for the Guru’s living presence as the necessary condition for hearing divine glory, pleading for intimate communion that transforms the self into a vessel of sacred sound. The teeka names the Guru as the one called, where the English leaves the guest unnamed.

Themes: invitation to the Beloved Guru, heart as inner sanctuary, receiving the Lord's Praises, sacred hearing, supplication for divine presence, spiritual intimacy, transformation through sacred sound
ਆਉ ਹਮਾਰੈ ਰਾਮ ਪਿਆਰੇ ਜੀਉ ॥:
A devotee begs the Beloved Lord to come and dwell inside their heart, making the inner self a home for divine presence. The utterance is a raw plea of longing that calls God inward to abide within rather than stay far away. It expresses aching desire for interior union, for the Divine to live within the core of the being.

Themes: divine indwelling, longing for union, invitation to the Beloved, heart as sacred dwelling, intimate devotion, interior presence, yearning for communion, God residing within
ਬਿਨਵੰਤਿ ਨਾਨਕ ਦਇਆ ਧਾਰਹੁ ਘਰਿ ਆਵਹੁ ਨਾਹ ਪਿਆਰ:
The soul-bride pleads with the Divine Husband to grant mercy and come live within her heart-home. It is an urgent cry for interior presence, begging the Beloved to turn the devotee’s inner being into his dwelling through grace. The stance is desperate supplication, pressing for union inside the private chamber of the self.

Themes: divine union, longing for grace, bridal mysticism, interiority of devotion, the heart as sacred dwelling, separation from the Beloved, desperate supplication
ਮੋਹਨ ਘਰਿ ਆਵਹੁ ਕਰਉ ਜੋਦਰੀਆ ॥:
The soul begs the enrapturing Beloved to come dwell within the heart’s chamber, treating that inner house not as a sealed lodging but as an open sanctuary for divine presence. It is a posture of desperate entreaty, pleading for inward union and intimate habitation rather than distant reverence, turning the self into a living abode where the Fascinating One alone resides.

Themes: inward union, divine indwelling, heart as sanctuary, longing for the Beloved, humble supplication, presence within the self, soul as divine abode
ਹਮ ਘਰਿ ਸਾਜਨ ਆਏ ॥:
The words suggest ordinary guests entering a house, yet the traditional commentary reads them mystically: the Friend, the Divine Beloved, has revealed Himself within the heart's interior home. The speaker announces an inward arrival, declaring that the Lord has made Himself manifest in the sanctuary of the self. This is jubilant recognition of divine presence taking residence inside the devotee's being.

Themes: divine indwelling, heart as sacred dwelling, God as intimate Friend, inward revelation, manifestation of the Beloved, joyous recognition, spiritual fulfillment
ਪਹਿਲੈ ਪਹਰੈ ਫੁਲੜਾ ਫਲੁ ਭੀ ਪਛਾ ਰਾਤਿ ॥:
Worship in the first night watch is only a flowering; the fruit of realization ripens in later watches, particularly amrit vela (the ambrosial hours). It admonishes seekers not to mistake preliminary beauty for completion, demanding the matured yield that ends the night’s labor. Early devotion blossoms; final devotion nourishes.
Themes: stages of devotion, amrit vela, spiritual maturation, preliminary worship, ripeness of realization, night watches, floral metaphor, fruit of discipline
ਕਬੀਰ ਸੂਤਾ ਕਿਆ ਕਰਹਿ ਉਠਿ ਕਿ ਨ ਜਪਹਿ ਮੁਰਾਰਿ:
Admonishing the self for squandering life in the drugged sleep of maya (worldly attachment). The image of sleeping indicts spiritual lethargy as fatal negligence, while waking demands immediate simran (loving remembrance) to shatter delusion. One must rouse the mind from mundane stupor into alert, conscious devotion before time runs out.
Themes: self-admonition, sleep of maya, waking for simran, urgency of remembrance, spiritual lethargy, alert devotion
ਪਰਭਾਤੇ ਪ੍ਰਭ ਨਾਮੁ ਜਪਿ ਗੁਰ ਕੇ ਚਰਣ ਧਿਆਇ ॥:
Instructing the seeker to rise in the ambrosial hours and adopt the discipline of naam (the divine Name) and simran (loving remembrance) while fixing the mind on the Guru's feet, the image of those feet signifies taking humble refuge in the teacher who unites the soul with the Divine. This command consecrates earliest consciousness to God through repetitive remembrance and complete surrender to the Guru's guidance, enshrining the Guru's presence with meekness in the heart.

Themes: amrit vela, naam simran, Guru's feet, humility, dawn discipline, surrender to the Guru, divine remembrance
ਝਾਲਾਘੇ ਉਠਿ ਨਾਮੁ ਜਪਿ ਨਿਸਿ ਬਾਸੁਰ ਆਰਾਧਿ ॥:
The instruction commands rising in the ambrosial hours before dawn to chant naam (the divine Name), yet it does not limit worship to that moment; it demands continuous remembrance through night and day. It exhorts making divine invocation the first act upon waking and the unbroken rhythm of life, turning every moment into an occasion for devotion rather than confining reverence to a single session.

Themes: amrit vela, daily discipline, chanting the Name, continuous remembrance, divine worship, uninterrupted devotion, dawn practice, perpetual adoration
ਬਾਬੀਹਾ ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤ ਵੇਲੈ ਬੋਲਿਆ ਤਾਂ ਦਰਿ ਸੁਣੀ ਪ:
The soul, imaged as a rainbird, utters its plea during amrit vela (the ambrosial hours before dawn), and that appeal is admitted to the Divine Court. The metaphor establishes that pre-dawn crying-out reaches the Creator; devotion offered in the early watch secures divine hearing. It urges rising in darkness to call upon God, assuring that such earnest petition is received at the threshold.

Themes: amrit vela, pre-dawn prayer, divine audience, soul as rainbird, supplication, spiritual discipline, answered prayer, God's court
ਛਾਤੀ ਸੀਤਲ ਮਨੁ ਸੁਖੀ ਛੰਤ ਗੋਬਿਦ ਗੁਨ ਗਾਇ ॥:
Singing words of divine praise cools the speaker’s heart and settles the mind into peace. The devotee declares that giving voice to glory ends inner heat and agitation, leaving the chest soothed and the self released. It testifies to the bodily calm and mental relief found through glorifying the Divine.

Themes: divine praise, heart-cooling, mental peace, relief from agitation, bodily calm, glorifying the Divine, devotional song, inner release
ਜੋਗੁ ਬਨਿਆ ਤੇਰਾ ਕੀਰਤਨੁ ਗਾਈ ॥੧॥:
Singing Your kirtan (singing of divine praises) is itself the attainment of true yoga; glorifying the Divine is not a step toward union but union itself. The speaker declares that both worldly contentment and the ascetic’s bliss are received inside this singing, collapsing every external discipline into a single act of loving praise.

Themes: kirtan as yoga, praise as union, devotional singing as ascetic accomplishment, worldly and spiritual bliss through glorification, collapse of external ritual into utterance, attainment through singing praises
ਹਉ ਅਨਦਿਨੁ ਹਰਿ ਨਾਮੁ ਕੀਰਤਨੁ ਕਰਉ ॥:
The devotee pledges unbroken worship, filling every moment from night to day with the inward repetition of naam (the divine Name) and the outward glorification through kirtan (singing the divine praises). This declares ceaseless meditation, constant divine praise, and total absorption in uninterrupted remembrance.

Themes: constant remembrance, unceasing kirtan, repetition of the divine Name, total devotion, divine praise, continuous worship, spiritual commitment, absorption in the Divine
ਰੁਣ ਝੁਣੋ ਸਬਦੁ ਅਨਾਹਦੁ ਨਿਤ ਉਠਿ ਗਾਈਐ ਸੰਤਨ ਕ:
Instruct the listener to rise each day and enter sangat (the company of the devout) to voice the unstruck divine melody that vibrates without instrument. The command prescribes dawn discipline of communal praise, urging the seeker to attune daily to the wordless music of reality through gathered worship and to make that collective song the axis of morning practice.

Themes: daily rising, sangat, unstruck melody, communal praise, dawn discipline, attunement to divine sound, instruction
ਸਾਧੋ ਗੋਬਿੰਦ ਕੇ ਗੁਨ ਗਾਵਉ ॥:
Addressing the sangat (the company of the devout), the utterance commands ceaseless singing of Gobind’s virtues. It exhorts turning every word into uninterrupted worship, making praise of the Lord of the Universe a constant discipline rather than a fleeting rite. The stance is urgent instruction to sanctify breath itself through continuous glorification.

Themes: continuous praise, divine virtues, exhortation to sangat, vocal worship, unbroken remembrance, glorification of Gobind, spiritual discipline
ਨਿਰਬਾਣ ਕੀਰਤਨੁ ਗਾਵਹੁ ਕਰਤੇ ਕਾ ਨਿਮਖ ਸਿਮਰਤ ਜ:
Sing the Creator's praises while abiding in nirvana, the desireless state beyond craving, for through its grace even one moment of simran (loving remembrance) liberates from vice. The counsel urges praise as a practice where instantaneous contemplation severs all bonds of corruption, declaring that a split second of remembrance alone grants final freedom.

Themes: nirvana, kirtan, simran, liberation from vice, instantaneous salvation, desirelessness, divine praise, remembrance
ਮਨ ਮੀਠ ਤੁਹਾਰੋ ਕੀਓ ॥੧॥ ਰਹਾਉ ॥:
The speaker bears witness that the Beloved's every act tastes sweet to the mind, a surrender so total they have never blamed anyone for any injury or excess. This image of sweetness signals a consciousness emptied of complaint, where embracing divine will dissolves every grievance against others. It declares a transformed perception that converts all occurrences, including harm done by people, into the Beloved's acceptable doing.
Themes: sweetness of divine will, total surrender, absence of blame, dissolution of grievance, transformed perception, acceptance of harm as God's doing, non-complaint toward others, egoless consciousness
ਮੀਤ ਕੇ ਕਰਤਬ ਕੁਸਲ ਸਮਾਨਾ ॥੧॥:
The speaker finds every deed of the Divine Friend as pleasant and comforting as ease itself. This declares total contentment with the Beloved's will, accepting each action with joy rather than resistance. To the devoted soul, whatever the Friend-Lord does feels like happiness and complete welfare.

Themes: contentment, Divine Friend, acceptance of the Beloved's will, joy in divine actions, ease and welfare, satisfaction, delight in God's deeds
ਸਰਬ ਸੁਖ ਆਨੰਦ ਮੰਗਲ ਰਸ ਮਾਨਿ ਗੋਬਿੰਦੈ ਆਗਿਓ ॥:
Surrender to the divine Will (raza) of the Lord of the Universe brings the speaker every comfort, bliss, and joy. Accepting that sweet command transforms life into unbroken celebration; total felicity follows from bowing to that supreme decree. This is a first-person declaration that obedience to the cosmic order is the immediate source of all happiness.

Themes: surrender to divine will, acceptance of God's command, bliss through obedience, total peace and joy, spiritual fulfillment, egoless submission
ਖਿਨ ਮਹਿ ਥਾਪਿ ਉਥਾਪਨਹਾਰਾ ਆਪਨ ਹਾਥਿ ਮਤਾਤ ॥੧॥:
The Divine establishes and annihilates in a single instant, holding every decision and destiny within His own hands. This asserts absolute sovereignty, declaring that all power to raise up or cast down belongs to God alone; nothing stands or falls by any will but His. Complete dependence on that omnipotent control is the only condition of existence.
Themes: divine omnipotence, instantaneous creation and destruction, absolute sovereignty, divine judgment, total dependence on divine will, God as sole arbiter, transience of worldly power
ਨਾਨਕ ਨਾਮੁ ਧਿਆਈਐ ਕਾਰਜੁ ਆਵੈ ਰਾਸਿ ॥੧॥:
Enshrine the naam (the divine Name) constantly in the mind, and every undertaking completes successfully. This instruction declares that sustained interior remembrance directly causes all affairs to resolve fruitfully. Keeping divine awareness alive within the self brings every task to its rightful end without dependence on outward effort alone.

Themes: naam, constant interior remembrance, enshrinement in the mind, success of undertakings, resolution of affairs, divine mindfulness, fruitful completion
ਕਾਰਜੁ ਤੇਰਾ ਹੋਵੈ ਪੂਰਾ ਹਰਿ ਹਰਿ ਹਰਿ ਗੁਣ ਗਾਇ:
Addressing the mind directly, the instruction exhorts the self to continually sing the divine virtues (gun) of Har in joyful praise, promising that this devotional practice alone will bring every undertaking to complete fruition and perfect resolution. It counsels the mind to abandon anxiety over worldly outcomes by making ceaseless praise the instrument through which all tasks succeed, assuring that chanting the Lord's glories necessarily fulfills life's true purpose.

Themes: self-exhortation addressed to the mind, continual singing of divine virtues (gun), certainty of bearing fruit, praise as the instrument of success, perfect resolution of all affairs, fulfillment of life's true purpose, chanting the glories of Har
ਨਾਨਕ ਨਾਮੁ ਅਰਾਧਣਾ ਕਾਰਜੁ ਆਵੈ ਰਾਸਿ ॥੮॥:
Adore and remember the divine Name, naam, through simran (loving remembrance). This prescription promises that every life-task and worldly affair achieves perfect resolution through such devotion. It commands inward remembrance and guarantees that spiritual devotion completes all undertakings, fulfills every purpose, and brings every enterprise to successful fruition.
Themes: naam, simran, resolution of affairs, successful completion, spiritual practice, divine remembrance, life's purpose, devotion
ਸਭੇ ਕਾਜ ਸਵਾਰਿਐ ਜਾ ਤੁਧੁ ਭਾਵੰਦਾ ॥੭॥:
All affairs are resolved and set in order only when they accord with Divine pleasure and sovereign will. No endeavor succeeds without God's favor; every task reaches fulfillment solely through alignment with that consent. The stance is grateful recognition that complete dependence on grace is the only cause of success in every matter.

Themes: Divine will, Divine pleasure, grace, dependence on God, resolution of affairs, success through God's favor, surrender
ਸਗਲ ਮਨੋਰਥ ਪੂਰਨ ਹੋਏ ਕਦੇ ਨ ਹੋਇ ਦੁਖਾਲਾ ਜੀਉ:
Every need and mental longing reaches perfect completion and sorrow never again afflicts the soul; whether the speaker testifies personally or depicts that blessed person, the utterance proclaims absolute contentment, the total satisfaction of all wishes, and permanent invulnerability to anguish as the sure fruit of such a life.

Themes: fulfillment of desires, cessation of sorrow, perfect contentment, spiritual completion, divine reward, unshakeable peace, permanent happiness, freedom from grief
